name: liminal-git
description: Native git operations for Node.js, built on libgit2 via napi-rs.
//files: Without this, npm falls back to .gitignore to decide what to pack — and .gitignore excludes *.node, because the addon is built on install rather than committed. The result was a package containing every Rust source file and no binding at all, failing on require with 'Cannot find native binding'. The Rust sources are not needed in the installed package: `prepare` runs in npm's own clone, which has the full checkout regardless of this list. THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is listed because it must travel with the compiled binary, which statically links libgit2 — npm adds LICENSE on its own but not this.

scripts.//prepare: Runs on `npm install` from a git URL, which is how Nocturne consumes this. The compiled addon is not committed, so without this a git install yields source and no binding. Requires a Rust toolchain and a C compiler on the installing machine — a deliberate choice: consumers build from source rather than being shipped binaries.
scripts.//test: --no-default-features is required, not a preference: with the napi feature on, a test binary fails at the linker because napi resolves its symbols from the host Node process at run time. `test:unit` and `test:integration` previously passed --features test-utils, a feature that does not exist in Cargo.toml, so both failed on their first line.
